To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hedonic and utilitational usage of Facebook are differentially related to browsing and participation in the community.

hedonic motivations are more strongly associated with participation in company-hosted Facebook page communities than are utilitarian motivations, whereas utilitarian motivations are more strongly linked to browsing than are hedonic motivations.

(1) hedonic motivations relate to community participation, (2) utilitarian motivations relate to community browsing, (3) browsing relates to purchase intentions, and (4) participation does not relate to purchase intentions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of hedonic and utilitarians motivations to use company-hosted Facebook page.
the question whether the company-hosted Facebook page can be used as a sales channel, and whether it is possible to get from liking to purchasing.
the effects of consumers’ underlying motivations for using company Facebook pages on their usage behavior and their effects on business outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hedonic motivations are more important for the community itself than for the company, while utilitarian motivations are more important in the context of the company.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the two motivations, hedonic and utilitari- an, have different implications for companies’ Facebook usage.
hedonic motivations lead to participation in the community and utilitarian motivations lead to merely browsing.
hedonic motivations are related to community participation, but that participation is not related to the company’s business performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the motivations of community members need to be considered in order to understand their behavior in the community and their effect on the company’s business.
companies need to understand that the two types of Facebook users (hedonic vs. utilitarian) have different needs and that these different types of users need to be treated differently.
hedonic motivations for using company Facebook pages are not necessarily related to buying from the company.
